From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: draft technical answers for Northstar — rollback + data-sync

Diego / Monica — draft details to paste into customer reply. Please edit for tone.

1) Rollback criteria (customer-facing summary)
- Automatic failover is performed when health checks indicate regional control-plane or network isolation beyond a configurable threshold (default 90s).
- Failover path: requests are routed to the secondary region by the smart routing layer; model variants that share the same KV schema are selected automatically.
- Rollback decision: automatic rollback is suppressed by default to avoid flip-flopping. Rollback to original primary occurs only after:
  a) primary region is healthy for a configurable monitoring window (default 15 minutes),
  b) no consistency anomalies detected in the data-sync audit (see point 3), and
  c) operator explicitly approves rollback in the Console (or via API) — we provide an optional auto-rollback flag for customers that want fully automated reversal after stability is observed.
- Human intervention: when auto-rollback is disabled, the operator will see a recommended rollback action with timeline and estimated client-impact in Console. Typical human approval window is < 10 minutes if net ops want to expedite.

2) Data sync and in-flight requests
- We use append-only sequence numbers for persistent request logs and per-shard replication markers for KV. During failover we:
  a) drain existing front-end request queues using a short-grace period (configurable, default 2s) to allow in-flight RPCs to complete where possible,
  b) switch new traffic to secondary, and
  c) replay uncommitted operations from the request log to the secondary using the sequence number watermark.
- RPO commitment: for our Dedicated tier with synchronous replication enabled, we target RPO <= 15s. For asynchronous replication (default on hosted tiers for cost-performance trade-offs) typical observed RPO is 15–120s; we provide workload-specific quantiles after a short sampling run.
- In-flight semantics: requests acknowledged to clients before switchover are guaranteed durable (persisted to the active region's write-ahead log). For in-flight requests that had not reached durability at the moment of switchover, we mark them in the audit stream and replay if idempotent; non-idempotent requests are surfaced to the application with a clear error code and a suggested retry pattern.
- Data fidelity checks: the audit pipeline produces a per-shard checksum+sequence watermark that the Console exposes in the post-failover report (CSV + JSON). We can share anonymized sample outputs.

3) Evidence and test artifacts
- We ship: runbook excerpt (failover decision tree), failover-rehearsal-summary (includes timelines and measured RTO/RPO), and an evidence matrix with event markers that map to log traces.
- Example logs: we include a short example that shows the sequence-watermark crossing and replay completion event (TIMESTAMP, SHARD, SEQ_START, SEQ_END, STATUS).

4) Limitations & recommended config
- If customers run large monolithic state in ephemeral caches without persistence or use non-idempotent writes, they should enable synchronous replication or place a small write-ack shim in front of critical writes.
- We recommend a rehearsal cadence (quarterly) and a targeted rehearsal that includes traffic shaping to mimic peak traffic.

I'll caveat the customer-facing copy with options for auto-rollback and the measured quantiles per workload.

—Rishi
Sr. Staff Engineer, Infra

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 12:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rollback criteria + data sync guarantees (clarifications)

Steve — quick answers:

1) Drain timeout is configurable per-route. For your long inference calls we recommend setting route-level graceful-drain = 20s for the rehearsal and 30s for production if you have flows that commonly run >10s. Note this increases the RTO window proportionally while preserving in-flight success rates.

2) Replay behavior depends on the persistence mode you select:
  - Synchronous replication: replay is synchronous for any operation that had the durability marker pending — the client will observe either a success or a deterministic retryable error.
  - Asynchronous replication: replay is performed as high-priority background reconciliation; clients may be returned a retryable error if the write had not been durably committed at switchover time. The audit report includes which sequence ranges were replayed and timestamps for reconciliation.

We can include a sample trace that shows the client-side error code to make compliance happy. We'll also schedule the rehearsal and provide the full trace, as Diego noted.

—Monica Patel
Principal, Reliability Solutions (Redwood Inference)
